final:
Checking the candidates with `klar contrast` (foreground on white) to confirm they pass 4.5.

Five accents, each measured with `klar contrast <color> "#ffffff"` (OKCA, foreground on background). All pass the 4.5 body-text threshold and all are in sRGB gamut:

| Role | Hex | OKCA on white |
|---|---|---|
| Red | `#a14843` | 4.7 |
| Amber | `#985409` | 4.7 |
| Green | `#347939` | 4.7 |
| Blue | `#4160a7` | 5.0 |
| Purple | `#814a8d` | 5.0 |

- **Hue spread:** the hues sit at roughly 25°, 60°, 145°, 265° and 320°, so they are clearly different from each other.
- **Teal option:** I also tested teal `#00747b` (4.8). I left it out because it sits close to the green and blue. It's a good swap if you'd rather have a cooler set.
- **Margins:** red, amber and green pass by only 0.2, so don't lighten them further.
- **Existing tokens:** I didn't change anything in `tokens.json`. Your current `success` (`oklch(0.7 0.3 150)`) and `danger` (`oklch(0.62 0.26 25)`) are out of sRGB gamut and much lighter than these. They would likely fail 4.5 as text on white, so I can check them if you want.

I couldn't fill a full 4×3 grid. `klar variants "#3b82f6" --light-steps 4 --chroma-steps 3` gives exactly 4×3, but only 3 of its 12 cells fit in sRGB. The other 9 come back with an empty color, so I left them out.

The rows below run light to dark and the columns run low, base and high chroma. Each score is OKCA with the shade as foreground on `#fff`, and body text needs 4.5.

| L \ C | 0.078 (low) | 0.188 (base) | 0.298 (high) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.873 | out of gamut | out of gamut | out of gamut |
| 0.623 | `#6b88b6` 2.9 ❌ | `#3b82f6` 2.9 ❌ | out of gamut |
| 0.373 | `#274069` 9.2 ✅ | out of gamut | out of gamut |
| 0.123 | out of gamut | out of gamut | out of gamut |

- **Passes:** only `#274069` (9.2).
- **Fails:** `#6b88b6` and your base `#3b82f6`, both at 2.9.

For a fully in-gamut grid, adaptive mode (`klar variants "#3b82f6"`) returns 7 rows by 3 columns. Its chroma columns are 0.008, 0.058 and 0.188, and the top column has only 2 shades because the base blue is near the gamut edge. It gives more passing shades:

| Shade | OKCA on white | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `#686b70` (low chroma) | 4.4 | ❌ just short |
| `#4a4d51` (low chroma) | 7.4 | ✅ |
| `#2a2c30` (low chroma) | 12.8 | ✅ |
| `#040507` (low chroma) | 19.4 | ✅ |
| `#3c506f` (mid chroma) | 7.1 | ✅ |
| `#1d2e4c` (mid chroma) | 12.3 | ✅ |
| `#000922` (mid chroma) | 18.7 | ✅ |

The high-chroma column has `#1e65d7` at 4.3, also just short. The passing shades are all L ≤ 0.43, so on white you need a much darker blue than `#3b82f6`.

I can pick 4 rows from the adaptive grid to get a 4×3, or use `klar find` to get the lightest shade of the base hue that reaches 4.5.

Use **`#7bacfc`** as the dark-mode primary. `klar contrast` scores it **4.5 OKCA** on `#1a1a2e`, which is exactly the AA body-text threshold. The brand `#3b82f6` scores only 1.9 on that surface.

| | Hex | OKLCH | OKCA on `#1a1a2e` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brand | `#3b82f6` | 0.62 / 0.19 / 259.8° | 1.9 (fails) |
| Dark-mode | `#7bacfc` | 0.74 / 0.13 / 259.85° | 4.5 (passes) |

The hue is the same, at about 259.8°. Lightness rises from 0.62 to 0.74, and chroma drops from 0.19 to 0.13, which is a ΔE of about 13. So it's a paler, slightly less saturated blue than the brand.

- **Saturation:** this is not a lightness-only fix. `klar find` without `--allow-desaturation` failed with `lightness-exhausted` and returned a color scoring 2.2. I ran it again with `--allow-desaturation`, which is what produced `#7bacfc`. You said "as close to the brand color as possible" but didn't say saturation could be reduced, so this is a judgment call on my part. Tell me if you want to keep the chroma.
- **`klar find`'s lightness-only result looks unreliable.** It gave up at 2.2, but lighter blues clearly pass: `#93c5fd` scores 7.3. Checking the output, `klar find` only reported a lightness-only result of 2.2, and I didn't investigate why it stopped there.
- **Other candidates:** `#79b1ff` scores 4.7 and `#75afff` scores 4.5. `#7bacfc` is the one `klar find` returned, and it keeps the brand hue almost exactly.
- **Margin:** 4.5 is right at the threshold. If you want headroom against rounding, use `#79b1ff` (4.7).

I haven't edited any token files. I can add this as the dark-mode value in `tokens.json` if you want.

final:
I audited `tokens-system.json` with `klar contrast` (OKCA, foreground on background, target 4.5). Most pairs fail. Five colors need a fix on one or both backgrounds. The fixes come from `klar find` (background fixed, foreground adjusted, target 4.5).

## Contrast (OKCA)

| Foreground | on `surface` #ffffff | on `surface-dark` #1a1a2e |
|---|---|---|
| text #1a1a2e | 15.8 ✅ | 1.0 (same color) |
| primary #3b82f6 | 2.9 ❌ | 1.9 ❌ |
| accent #e94560 | 2.8 ❌ | 2.0 ❌ |
| success #22c55e | 1.9 ❌ | 3.4 ❌ |
| muted #666666 | 4.8 ✅ | 2.4 ❌ |
| inverse #ffffff | 1.0 (same color) | 16.5 ✅ |

`text` on `surface-dark` and `inverse` on `surface` are identical colors, so they are never valid pairings. I'm treating them as "don't use", not as fixes.

## Proposed fixes

ΔE is klar's own figure for how far the color moves. Most fixes land above 4.5 by a small margin because `find` accepts a small overshoot.

| Pair | Fix | New contrast | ΔE | What changes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| primary on surface | #3b82f6 → **#115bcc** | 5.0 | 15 | Lightness only, hue and chroma kept |
| accent on surface | #e94560 → **#bf103f** | 4.7 | 13 | Lightness only |
| success on surface | #22c55e → **#047f38** | 4.6 | 22 | Lightness and chroma (0.19 → 0.14) |
| primary on surface-dark | #3b82f6 → **#7bacfc** | 4.5 | 13 | Lightness and chroma (0.19 → 0.13), noticeably paler |
| accent on surface-dark | #e94560 → **#fe8a93** | 4.6 | 14 | Lightness and chroma (0.20 → 0.14), turns salmon pink |
| success on surface-dark | #22c55e → **#41d870** | 4.8 | 5 | Lightness only, a small nudge |
| muted on surface-dark | #666666 → **#919191** | 4.7 | 17 | Lightness only, still neutral gray |

## Things to decide

- **Two values per token.** Primary, accent and success each need a light-surface value and a dark-surface value, since no single color passes on both. Muted (#666666) passes on white as is and only needs a lighter variant for dark.
- **Desaturation is a design call.** Four of the fixes (success on light, primary on dark, accent on dark) can't reach 4.5 by lightness alone. klar reports `lightness-exhausted` for them, and I applied `--allow-desaturation` to get the values above. Lightness alone only gets these to about 2.2–2.8. If you'd rather keep the brand saturation, the alternative is using those colors only for non-text or large-text elements. I haven't checked them against a lower threshold.
- **Nothing was changed.** I only audited. I haven't edited `tokens-system.json`, and the README says `tokens.json` is the source of truth, so tell me if you want the fixes applied there.
